task: Add concurrency guards to GitHub Actions workflows so a rapid push does not leave duplicate/overlapping CI runs on the same ref

events.summary: Workflow-file edits only; no cmd/internal/charts/Dockerfile/scripts runtime logic touched

Confirmed via grep that dependabot-licenses.yaml was the only workflow with a concurrency block (group keyed on the PR number, cancel-in-progress false); the remaining workflows in .github/workflows/ had none

Added concurrency: {group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: <expr|false>} to every push/pull_request-triggered workflow lacking one, matching the dasomel/openforge house convention

cancel-in-progress scoped per event type, not per workflow: agent-behavior, ci, codeql and e2e-airgap use ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }} so only superseded PR runs are cancelled, because push/schedule/workflow_dispatch all have a null pull_request.number and collapse onto refs/heads/main. cleanup-merged-branch, scorecard and release keep a literal false (they mutate external state: branch deletion, Sigstore-signed result publication, release image push/signing)
All edited YAML files parsed cleanly with python3 yaml.safe_load before commit; PR CI triggered the edited workflows themselves, confirming GitHub Actions also parses them without error

Independent critic pass (Claude Opus reviewer plus a Gemini lane, in contexts that did not author the change) rejected the first revision: a literal cancel-in-progress true would have let a workflow_dispatch cancel the weekly Air-Gap E2E run, which uploads no artifacts and is the project's only real-kernel xfs/ext4/btrfs enforcement evidence; the same collapse applied to codeql's weekly scan and to ci.yaml, which is not scan-only (it uploads SARIF to code scanning and reports to Codecov). Both reviewers' findings were reproduced against the workflow files before the expression fix was applied

Concurrency guards added to 7 workflows; dependabot-licenses.yaml (already had one) and publish-openforge-status.yml (workflow_dispatch-only, no push/pull_request trigger) left untouched. Known and deliberately not addressed here: cleanup-merged-branch.yml's group key includes the PR number, so repo-wide sweeps triggered by different PRs still do not serialize -- harmless today because the sweep is idempotent and tolerates an already-deleted ref, but its group key does not achieve the queueing its rationale describes
